newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First sees no block to tertiary funds decision.
newsitem.headline: NZ First sees no block to tertiary funds decision.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday said tertiary education funding decisions should be made as quickly as possible.

Caretaker Education Minister Wyatt Creech told Radio New Zealand he expects tertiary funding decisions for the next year will be made within the next two weeks after he has carried out consultation with other parties under the conventions of caretaker government.
Some tertiary institutions have said delays in funding confirmation are threatening courses.
"New Zealand First won't be reducing the level of funding therefore it cannot see any reason why the money shouldn't be approved," Peters said in a statement.
Creech has acknowledged decisions on funding would normally have been made by the end of October but says this was impossible due to the timing of the election on October 12.
